--- title: "Risk-Aware Decision Making" description: "Use ConformalRiskControl with custom risk functions for cost-sensitive predictions." date: today format: html: self-contained: true embed-resources: true code-fold: true code-tools: true --- Standard conformal prediction controls **coverage probability** — but real decisions often care about **cost**. This notebook shows how to use `ConformalRiskControl` with custom risk functions: - **Inventory management** — stockouts cost 10x more than excess inventory - **Asymmetric loss** — underpredictions penalized more than overpredictions - **Threshold penalty** — large errors are catastrophic We demonstrate all three scenarios, starting with the **inventory** scenario as the primary example. ::: {#setup .cell cache='true' execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import numpy as np import polars as pl from sklearn.ensemble import GradientBoostingRegressor from uncertainty_flow.risk import ( ConformalRiskControl, asymmetric_loss, inventory_cost, threshold_penalty, ) from uncertainty_flow.utils.split import select_validation_plan from uncertainty_flow.wrappers import ConformalRegressor ``` ::: ::: {#cell-load-data .cell cache='true' execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} df = pl.read_parquet("../data/energy_efficiency.parquet") print(f"Shape: {df.shape}") df.head(5) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Shape: (768, 10) ``` ::: ::: {#load-data .cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ::: {#split-data .cell cache='true' execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} cols = df.columns target_col = cols[-1] plan = select_validation_plan(df, task_type="tabular", holdout_fraction=0.15, random_state=42) train_val, test_df = plan.outer_split n_calib = len(train_val) * 15 // 85 train_df = train_val[:-n_calib] if n_calib else train_val calib_df = train_val[-n_calib:] if n_calib else train_val[:0] print(f"Plan: {plan.metadata.strategy_name} | Train: {len(train_df)} | Calib: {len(calib_df)} | Test: {len(test_df)}") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Plan: random_holdout | Train: 538 | Calib: 115 | Test: 115 ``` ::: ::: ## Scenario 1: Inventory Cost Stockouts cost $10/unit, holding costs $1/unit. We control expected inventory cost per prediction. ::: {#cell-scenario-inventory .cell cache='true' execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} target_risk = 0.1 risk_fn_inventory = inventory_cost(holding_cost=1.0, stockout_cost=10.0) base_model = ConformalRegressor( base_model=GradientBoostingRegressor(random_state=42), auto_tune=False, random_state=42, ) base_model.fit(train_df, target=target_col) risk_model_inventory = ConformalRiskControl( base_model=base_model, risk_function=risk_fn_inventory, target_risk=target_risk, random_state=42, ) risk_model_inventory.fit(calib_df, target=target_col) risk_pred_inventory = risk_model_inventory.predict(test_df.drop(target_col)) risk_pred_inventory.head(10) ``` ::: {#scenario-inventory .cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ```{=html}

Useful when missing high values is expensive. ::: {#cell-scenario-asymmetric .cell cache='true' execution_count=7} ``` {.python .cell-code} risk_fn_asymmetric = asymmetric_loss(overprediction_penalty=1.0, underprediction_penalty=3.0) risk_model_asymmetric = ConformalRiskControl( base_model=base_model, risk_function=risk_fn_asymmetric, target_risk=target_risk, random_state=42, ) risk_model_asymmetric.fit(calib_df, target=target_col) risk_pred_asymmetric = risk_model_asymmetric.predict(test_df.drop(target_col)) risk_pred_asymmetric.head(10) ``` ::: {#scenario-asymmetric .cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=7} ```{=html}

Models the cost of catastrophic mispredictions. ::: {#cell-scenario-threshold .cell cache='true' execution_count=9} ``` {.python .cell-code} risk_fn_threshold = threshold_penalty(threshold=5.0, penalty_above=10.0, penalty_below=1.0) risk_model_threshold = ConformalRiskControl( base_model=base_model, risk_function=risk_fn_threshold, target_risk=target_risk, random_state=42, ) risk_model_threshold.fit(calib_df, target=target_col) risk_pred_threshold = risk_model_threshold.predict(test_df.drop(target_col)) risk_pred_threshold.head(10) ``` ::: {#scenario-threshold .cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=9} ```{=html}
